package_info.why_malicious: The package is part of a large-scale, coordinated spam campaign designed to game the Tea protocol's reward system. Thousands of nearly identical, non-functional or minimally functional packages are published under random names, with artificial dependency networks, to inflate 'teaRank' and farm cryptocurrency rewards. This pollutes the npm ecosystem, increases the risk of accidental dependency on malicious or useless code, and undermines trust in open source software.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At publish-time, the package.json declares thousands of dependencies on other spam packages from the same campaign, artificially inflating the dependency graph and teaRank score, with the outcome of maximizing protocol rewards.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages rarely have thousands of dependencies, especially on other obscure or non-functional packages. This pattern is a hallmark of ecosystem gaming.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages declare only necessary dependencies for functionality. Here, dependencies are used to manipulate ranking algorithms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Large meta-packages or frameworks may have many dependencies, but not in this random, interconnected, and non-functional manner.
key_indicators: Thousands of dependencies on similarly named, low-quality packages
No meaningful code or utility provided

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At publish-time, a tea.yaml file is included to register the package with the Tea protocol, enabling it to participate in the reward system and receive TEA tokens.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of tea.yaml in thousands of otherwise empty or non-functional repositories is a clear indicator of automated, reward-seeking spam.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate projects may use tea.yaml for protocol registration, but not in mass-produced, non-functional packages.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate open source projects using Tea protocol for rewards.
key_indicators: tea.yaml present in empty or near-empty repositories
Unique codeOwner addresses for each spam package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At publish-time, a minimal or meaningless README.md is included to give the appearance of a legitimate project, but provides no documentation or utility.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README files are expected to provide documentation. Here, they are used as filler to pass basic repository checks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Initial scaffolding for new projects, but not at this scale or with this intent.
key_indicators: README.md with only the package name or random text
No actual documentation or usage instructions

attack_chain.action: Automated creation of thousands of fake npm packages with random names and minimal content.
attack_chain.leads_to: Mass registration of packages with the Tea protocol.

attack_chain.action: Each package declares thousands of dependencies on other spam packages, creating a dense, interconnected dependency graph.
attack_chain.leads_to: Artificial inflation of teaRank scores for all involved packages.

attack_chain.action: Each package includes a tea.yaml file to register for TEA token rewards.
attack_chain.leads_to: Eligibility for protocol rewards and further incentive to publish more spam.

attack_chain.action: Fake or minimal README files are added to pass repository checks and appear legitimate.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages are accepted by npm and Tea protocol, completing the spam cycle.

behavioral_signatures: Packages with thousands of dependencies, especially on other obscure or low-download packages
Presence of tea.yaml in otherwise empty or non-functional repositories
Mass publication of packages with random, hyphenated names or Latin portmanteaus
file_indicators: tea.yaml present in root of repository
README.md with only package name or random text
network_indicators: High volume of npm publish events from the same or related accounts
Registration of packages with the Tea protocol (tea.xyz endpoints)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages with unusually high numbers of dependencies, especially if those dependencies are also low-quality or recently published. Flag repositories containing tea.yaml with minimal or no actual code. Detect mass publication patterns (e.g., many packages from the same user or with similar naming schemes). Correlate with Tea protocol registration activity to identify reward-farming campaigns.
